references.text: The background to Jephthah's words: his brothers drove him away because he was the son of a prostitute woman, and they denied him an inheritance in his father's house.
Isaac asked Abimelek and his men a similar question; they had previously shown him hostility but now came to seek peace with him.
Joseph was hated by his brothers, a parallel to how Jephthah was hated and driven away by his relatives.
Joseph's brothers came to him in distress after having wronged him earlier, a situation parallel to the elders of Gilead who now seek Jephthah's help.
Jesus quotes Psalm 118 about the stone that the builders rejected but which became the cornerstone—a theme concerning the rejected one being raised up.
Stephen recounts how Joseph was sold by his brothers but later became their savior—a pattern resembling Jephthah's story.
